description: Behaviour parameters for the day builder (map-client/src/sim/sourceDay.ts). Base values equal the builder's own constants (including its stable personal habits); modifiers apply when the day's conditions hold (calibration first, then conditions). Values are composed by paramsFor() in src/sim/behavior.ts and only ever change people's timelines, never counts or capacities. Calibration values are refitted locally by `npm run calibrate` (scripts/calibrate-behavior.mjs) against measured BU data.

modifiers.label: Meals peak at real meal times

provenance.note: Bell-shaped arrivals centred on 11:30–13:30 lunch and 17:30–19:30 dinner; centres fitted to dining-hall timing targets and BU Dining's published daily meal counts.

modifiers.label: Dining volume matches BU Dining's meal counts

provenance.note: Three main dining halls serve about 3,000 breakfasts, 5,000 lunches and 5,000 dinners a day (BU Today, 2017).

modifiers.label: Visits move into free gaps instead of being dropped

provenance.note: A clash with a class used to drop the meal or study session (18k rejected visits on a Wednesday); now it moves to the nearest free gap in its window. Visit lengths vary ±40%.

Library entries by hour fitted to the shape of the School of Theology Library's historical gate counts (the only BU library series in the data), with evening sessions kept so libraries stay occupied late.

modifiers.label: Library study follows the day, not just the evening

provenance.note: Library entries by hour fitted to the shape of the School of Theology Library's historical gate counts (the only BU library series in the data), with evening sessions kept so libraries stay occupied late.

modifiers.label: Weekday gym visits match FitRec's measured totals

provenance.note: FitRec's published hourly entries for Oct 17–23, 2026 total about 4,000 per weekday; the uncalibrated model produced about 1,400.

modifiers.label: Commuters stay on campus between classes

provenance.note: Commuters used to bounce through a transit stop for any 30-minute gap. They now wait on campus for gaps under a few hours and may visit before or after their classes. Walk-in access points near each destination and on-campus study blocks come from the day builder itself.

modifiers.label: People walk at different speeds and linger after class

provenance.note: Walking speeds of young adults average about 1.35 m/s with a standard deviation near 0.2 m/s (Bohannon 1997); 0–8 minutes of lingering after class removes the lockstep wave at the bell.

modifiers.label: Students spend free time by the river

provenance.note: No counts of people on BU Beach or the Esplanade exist in the data, so these shares are assumptions: about one in twelve residents spends a while on the grass on an ordinary dry weekday and one in twenty walks or runs the river path; commuters about a third as often. River time is a habit like the builder's others: 40% are regulars on the grass (×2) and 25% are river-path runners (×3), with everyone else lowered to keep the mean.
Weekends: late morning to sunset on the grass, longer stays, more runs.

Rain keeps students indoors: longer library stays, fewer outings and off-campus meals, faster and more direct walking. Direction follows studies of weather and pedestrian volumes (e.g. Aultman-Hall et al. 2009); sizes are assumptions.
Storms: students shelter indoors and skip optional trips. Sizes are assumptions.
Snow slows walking (about 15%), people leave earlier, some skip class and a few commuters stay home. Sizes are assumptions.
Heat: fewer midday outings, more time in air-conditioned libraries and dining halls (11:00–16:00 visits only).
Heat slows walking slightly and trims workouts. Sizes are assumptions.
Below 32°F students eat on campus more and linger less outside. Sizes are assumptions.
No classes during BU's Study Period (published calendar); studying replaces them. Sizes are assumptions.
Regular classes stop for finals (published calendar). Exam sittings are not published per room, so about 30% of class slots stand in for exams; libraries fill. Sizes are assumptions.
Classes suspended (published calendar); most students leave. Away shares are assumptions.
A single suspended class day (published calendar): residents sleep in, few commuters come in. Sizes are assumptions.
Before the first class residents settle in: dining halls busy, errands off campus, libraries quiet. Sizes are assumptions.
Patriots' Day: the course passes Kenmore Square next to campus around midday; many residents go out to watch. Sizes are assumptions.
Almost nobody sits on wet grass; a few runners still go out.
Nobody stays by the river in a thunderstorm.
Snow: no sitting out; some walk the river path.
Below 32°F hardly anyone sits outside.
32–55°F: fewer and shorter stays on the grass.
72–85°F and dry: BU Beach and the Esplanade fill up in the afternoon and evening.
In a heatwave people avoid the midday sun by the river.
Study breaks on the grass between library sessions.
Less free time during exams.

search.method: Seeded random search (¼ of the budget) then coordinate descent with step halving; acceptance requires every metric’s loss to rise by at most the tolerance and the weighted total to fall; winner confirmed on the full roster.
